title: Oily Opaque Malaysian Squid Noodles
description: A romantic Malaysian dish featuring squid, this recipe is a cultured and glassy-jelly delight, friendly to those following a low FODMAP diet. It combines the tender squid with noodles and flavorful ingredients.

ingredients.name: squid tubes
ingredients.notes: cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: garlic-infused oil
ingredients.notes: use garlic-free for strict FODMAP diets

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the rice noodles according to the package instructions, then set aside.
In a large skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Add the squid pieces to the skillet and cook until they are opaque and lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Remove the squid from the skillet and set aside with the noodles.
In the same skillet, add the garlic-infused oil, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil, stirring to combine.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer the sauce for about 2 minutes, until it thickens slightly.
Add the cooked noodles and squid back into the skillet, tossing everything to coat with the sauce.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the Oily Opaque Malaysian Squid Noodles hot, garnished with sliced green onions if desired.
